claims.title: What has to extend from the generic fibre?
claims.hypotheses: Marked integral models and a specified translation between their generic towers are given. Two comparison maps identify the respective generic families and their bases.
claims.statement: A map of bases and a map of universal total spaces extending the two generic squares give the prescribed translation on every fibre power. The composition of an h-step followed by an h′-step has label h′h.

claims.title: How can the same quotient give the wrong marking?
claims.hypotheses: On ℂ/ℤ[i] use the isogeny 1+i, fine level fourteen and target level seven. Each Gaussian integer represents a finite-level lattice label.
claims.statement: The quotient has a two-element kernel. The representative 1−i gives the prescribed marking, whereas 1+i permutes the same set of target points by the nontrivial unit i.

claims.title: Which marked points form the kernel of a lattice translation?
claims.hypotheses: The translation preserves the completed lattice, its image contains κ times that lattice, and the marked integer level Nκ is admissible at the two primes. The generic isogeny has the prescribed action on geometric Tate markings.
claims.statement: An integral representative F of κh⁻¹ at the fine level carries the source labels to the prescribed target labels. The kernel of the generic isogeny is exactly the marked subgroup generated by the classes at NFx.

claims.title: How does quotienting by these sections extend the marked isogeny?
claims.hypotheses: Compatible levels and ideal markings are fixed on the locally Noetherian unitary moduli model. The source carries the coefficient action, normalized polarization, Tate structure and free action by the finite subgroup of marked translations.
claims.statement: The finite quotient with the descended coefficient and polarization data, integer marking and ideal marking represents the translated object. Its map of total families realizes the required generic isogeny.

claims.title: How do the two ends of an elementary isogeny acquire integral models?
claims.hypotheses: The multiplicity-one unitary model is smooth and quasi-projective over a characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring. The integer level is at least three and prime to q. The elementary generic correspondence and both directional valuative and specialization controls are given.
claims.statement: The finite normalization in the generic source cover gives the source projection. The generic target projection extends over that model and is finite.

claims.title: Why do the isogeny and its reverse companion extend?
claims.hypotheses: The source of the elementary correspondence is locally Noetherian and normal. The pulled-back abelian schemes with their generic elementary isogeny and its companion are fixed.
claims.statement: Both homomorphisms extend. Their two composites are multiplication by the prescribed multiplier on the whole base, and the coefficient and level identities extend as well.

claims.title: How can the polarizing bundles be compared on the special fibre?
claims.hypotheses: The two polarizing line bundles on the common square are birigidified. Their pullback comparison at the prescribed multiplier holds on the dense open and both bundles restrict trivially to the double zero section.
claims.statement: The difference of the two classes is trivial. This gives the required isomorphism of line bundles on the integral model.

claims.title: When does a map on the generic cover extend to the integral base?
claims.hypotheses: A smooth scheme over a discrete valuation ring has a finite étale surjection onto its generic fibre. A map on that cover lies over a fixed map to the base of a finite target and agrees at every pair of geometric lifts.
claims.statement: The map descends to the generic fibre and extends uniquely to the smooth integral model over the prescribed base map.

claims.title: Which two maps descend for the elementary operator?
claims.hypotheses: The elementary operator at a prime above the selected split factor has integral lattice action and index j≤n. The source ideal is contained in the target ideal times the prime. The marked generic levels and divisibility by the j-th power of the ideal norm are as specified.
claims.statement: The class of the elementary kernel descends through the generic marking cover, followed by the full target marking. Pulling back the universal elementary isogeny produces the integral map of total families.
